full_text_en:
Cao Yasha, Liu Jinxiang — Financial Instrument Fraud Case

Defendant: Cao Yasha, female, 40 years old, manager of Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. (sole proprietorship), Shandong Province. Arrested on October 8, 1996.

Defense Counsel: Li Hongwei, lawyer from Weifang Dapeng Law Firm.

Defendant: Liu Jinxiang, male, 39 years old, from Gaomi City, Shandong Province, unemployed. Arrested on November 13, 1996.

Defense Counsel: Zhang Yonghua and Hao Hongjun, lawyers from Weifang Tongxin Law Firm.

The Weifang City People's Procuratorate, Shandong Province, initiated a public prosecution against defendants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang for the crime of financial instrument fraud before the Weifang Intermediate People's Court.

The Weifang Intermediate People's Court, after public trial, found the following facts:

Defendants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang, in order to use other people's funds, induced others to deposit money by offering to bring deposits to banks, a monthly interest rate of 21‰, paying the portion exceeding the normal bank interest rate to depositors in advance, or paying "kickbacks" to intermediaries. On May 21, 1996, Liu Jinxiang obtained a bank draft of RMB 10 million from the Shandong Provincial Finance Treasury Bond Service Department through an intermediary. Cao Yasha, through Li Chunbao, head of the Corporate Deposit Section of the Bank of China Weifang Branch (hereinafter referred to as Weifang Branch), handed this draft to the Corporate Deposit Section. Then, taking advantage of Li Chunbao's dereliction of duty, they transferred out RMB 9 million in the form of draft authorization letters, and deposited the remaining RMB 1 million into Weifang Branch under a personal name as a deposit attraction task completed by Li Chunbao for the branch. From the transferred funds, Cao Yasha paid an interest differential of RMB 1.062 million to the Shandong Provincial Finance Treasury Bond Service Department, paid "kickbacks" of RMB 490,000 to intermediaries, lent RMB 4.279 million to others at high interest, and deposited the remaining RMB 3.169 million into accounts opened by Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. at the Development Zone Construction Bank and Weifang Branch. Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang altered a time deposit certificate of lump-sum deposit and withdrawal with a face value of RMB 100 and a one-year term from Weifang Branch into a time deposit certificate with a face value of RMB 10 million and a one-year term, and handed it to the Shandong Provincial Finance Treasury Bond Service Department.

On July 19 of the same year, defendant Cao Yasha, using the same method, obtained a bank draft of RMB 5 million issued by Zhaoyuan City Rural Credit Cooperative through an intermediary. To obtain this remittance, Cao Yasha, together with her brother Cao Zhengjun (at large), found Gao Haiyan, an accountant at the Business Hall of Weifang Branch, and used a set of voided "Bank of China Special Transfer Vouchers" with complete seals provided by Gao Haiyan to deposit the RMB 5 million draft into the Business Department of Weifang Branch. Subsequently, Cao Yasha and Cao Zhengjun, through Gao Haiyan, retrieved the draft, filled in the endorsement transfer content in the endorsement column, and "transferred" the draft to Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. Cao Yasha and Cao Zhengjun altered a "Bank of China Time Deposit Certificate of Lump-Sum Deposit and Withdrawal" with a face value of RMB 50 into a bank deposit certificate with a face value of RMB 5 million, and handed it together with an interest differential of RMB 1.621 million to Zhaoyuan City Rural Credit Cooperative, in addition to paying "kickbacks" of RMB 190,000 to intermediaries. The remaining funds were used to repay the loan principal and interest owed by Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. to the bank.

On July 26 of the same year, defendant Cao Yasha, still using the same method, obtained two bank drafts of RMB 5 million each from Zhaoyuan City Foreign Supply Co., Ltd. and handed them to Weifang Branch. Together with Cao Zhengjun, she altered two "Bank of China Time Deposit Certificates of Lump-Sum Deposit and Withdrawal" each with a face value of RMB 50 into bank deposit certificates with a face value of RMB 5 million each, and handed them to Zhaoyuan City Foreign Supply Co., Ltd. Subsequently, Cao Yasha, together with others, forged an entrusted investment agreement and privately engraved the seals of the depositor and the savings accountant of the Bank of China, attempting to withdraw RMB 10 million from the bank, but the fraud was unsuccessful due to the case being uncovered.

In summary, defendant Cao Yasha committed three frauds by altering bank deposit certificates, with a total fraud amount of RMB 25 million (of which RMB 10 million was unsuccessful). Defendant Liu Jinxiang participated in one fraud. Cao Yasha used the defrauded money to pay interest differentials, intermediaries' "kickbacks", repay loans owed by Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. to the bank, and purchase cars, among other things. After the case was uncovered, the recovered cash and stolen goods totaled approximately RMB 12.0541 million, with over RMB 2.9458 million unable to be recovered.

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence such as seized altered bank deposit certificates, bank drafts, bank deposit slips, forensic science and technology examination conclusions, and witness testimony. Defendants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang also confessed, which is sufficient for determination.

The Weifang Intermediate People's Court held that defendants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang, in disregard of national law, with the intent of illegal possession, defrauded funds by altering bank instruments, with an extraordinarily large amount of fraud, severely disrupting financial order and causing particularly significant losses to the interests of the state and the people. Their conduct constituted the crime of instrument fraud under Articles 194 and 199 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and should be severely punished according to law. Given that Liu Jinxiang only participated in one fraud, he may receive a lighter punishment. Accordingly, the Weifang Intermediate People's Court, on October 13, 1997, rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Cao Yasha is convicted of instrument fraud and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life, and a fine of RMB 100,000;
2. Defendant Liu Jinxiang is convicted of instrument fraud and sentenced to life imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for life, and a fine of RMB 200,000.

After the first-instance judgment, defendants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang appealed to the Shandong High People's Court, both on the ground that the "sentence was too heavy." Cao Yasha's defense counsel argued that the first fraud was personally committed by Liu Jinxiang, and Cao Yasha was merely used by Liu Jinxiang; as for the second sum of money, there was insufficient evidence to prove that Cao Yasha had a clear subjective intent to defraud and no intention to repay in the future, and the funds were used to pay interest differentials, company loans, and intermediaries' "kickbacks," not squandered, and all expenditures were recovered; the third fraud was unsuccessful and should be given a lighter punishment.

The Shandong High People's Court, upon second-instance trial, held that the facts found in the original trial were clear, and the evidence was reliable and sufficient. Appellants Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang, with the intent of illegal possession, induced deposits with high interest rates, and after obtaining the deposits, used altered bank deposit certificates to deceive the depositors' trust, defrauding the depositors of an extraordinarily large amount of funds, disrupting the national financial order, and causing significant losses to the interests of the state and the people. Their conduct violated Articles 194 and 199 of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of financial instrument fraud. The original trial's conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. The appeal grounds of Cao Yasha and Liu Jinxiang and the opinions of their defense counsel could not be sustained. Accordingly, the Shandong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 189, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, on February 12, 1998, ruled to reject the appeal and sustain the original judgment. At the same time, pursuant to Article 200, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the case was reported to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

After review, the Supreme People's Court held:

Defendant Cao Yasha, together with co-defendant Liu Jinxiang, used altered bank deposit certificates to defraud funds in 1996, which violated Article 12, Paragraph 2 of the "Decision on Punishing Crimes Undermining the Financial Order" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision") promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on June 30, 1995, and constituted a crime. The charge for this paragraph was determined as "instrument fraud" in Article 5, Paragraph 4 of the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Adjudicating Fraud Cases" (hereinafter referred to as Fa Fa [1996] No. 32) issued by the Supreme People's Court on December 16, 1996. Article 194, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law, which came into effect on October 1, 1997, has the same content as Article 12, Paragraph 2 of the "Decision." Given that the "Law of the People's Republic of China on Negotiable Instruments" explicitly defines "negotiable instruments" as drafts, promissory notes, and checks, the Supreme People's Court, in the "Provisions on Determining Charges under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China" issued on December 9, 1997, determined the charge under Article 194, Paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law as "financial instrument fraud." The two judicial interpretations conflict on the determination of the charge. Pursuant to Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's "Notice on Earnestly Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Revised Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China," the conflicting part of the old judicial interpretation is no longer applicable. The crime committed by Cao Yasha was financial instrument fraud, and the original trial's determination of instrument fraud was improper and should be corrected.

Although defendant Cao Yasha was the manager of Weifang Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd., her financial instrument fraud criminal conduct was all carried out in her personal name and was unrelated to Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. The fact that Cao Yasha used part of the stolen funds to repay loans owed by Haizhou Industrial Co., Ltd. to the bank was merely personal use of the stolen proceeds and was also unrelated to a unit crime.

Defendant Cao Yasha defrauded others of RMB 25 million by altering financial instruments. Except for the unsuccessful fraud of RMB 10 million, only approximately RMB 12.0541 million in cash and stolen goods were recovered after the case was uncovered, and over RMB 2.9458 million could not be recovered due to personal squandering, causing particularly significant losses to the interests of the state and the people. Fa Fa [1996] No. 32 provides: "If an individual defrauds an amount of more than RMB 100,000 in instrument fraud, it constitutes an 'extraordinarily large amount'." The penalty prescribed in Article 12 of the "Decision" is: "If the amount is extraordinarily large or there are other particularly serious circumstances, the person shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death, and shall also have property confiscated." "Other particularly serious circumstances" in this context refers to circumstances such as squandering the defrauded property, making it impossible to recover, and causing particularly significant losses to the interests of the state and the people. Article 199 of the Criminal Law provides: "If a person commits a crime under Articles 192, 194, or 195 of this Section, and the amount is extraordinarily large and causes particularly significant losses to the interests of the state and the people, the person shall be sentenced to life imprisonment or death, and shall also have property confiscated." Comparing the two, there is no substantive difference in the sentencing conditions for the crime of financial instrument fraud between the "Decision" and the Criminal Law, and the prescribed penalties are consistent. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Criminal Law, this case should be convicted and punished under the "Decision." Neither Article 12 of the "Decision" nor Article 199 of the Criminal Law provides for a fine for the crime of financial instrument fraud. Therefore, the original trial's imposition of a fine on Cao Yasha was improper and should be amended. In summary, the facts found in the first-instance judgment and the second-instance ruling were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, and the trial procedure was lawful, but the application of law in terms of conviction and the imposition of a fine was improper. Accordingly, the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to Article 285, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," on March 6, 1999, rendered the following judgment:

1. The part of the first-instance criminal judgment and the second-instance criminal ruling concerning the conviction of defendant Cao Yasha and the imposition of a fine are vacated.
2. Defendant Cao Yasha is convicted of financial instrument fraud and sentenced to death, with deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property.
